quote: You only live twice: / Once when you are born / And once when you look death in the face.
source: Ian Fleming, You Only Live Twice, the epigraph, the verse Bond writes in chapter 11, Anatomy Class (Jonathan Cape, 1964)
note: Corrected the tag to Fiction and the source line. The verse is Fleming’s own: Bond writes it for Tiger in chapter 11 and Tiger says it has the wrong number of syllables for a haiku. The After Basho credit on the epigraph page is Fleming’s conceit, and no Basho poem stands behind it.

evidence.where: Local plain text of the novel (scratchpad yolt.txt, from the digital copy the first verifier used), grepped this run: the epigraph page prints the three lines with a full stop, credited After BASHO, Japanese poet, 1643-94; chapter 11, Anatomy Class, has Bond compose it and Tiger reject it as a haiku. Not the Cape 1964 page itself
evidence.edition: Jonathan Cape, 1964 (text read in an unofficial digital copy)
